Root AGENTS.md (AGENTS.md) references the spec via hyphenated file paths ('mcp-server/docs/agents/workflow-specification/') and the phrase 'workflow logic' — but not 'workflow specification' as a two-word phrase. No regression risk identified. All five files are documentation-only; no code was changed. The governance principle is consistently embedded regardless of the search-phrase observation above.

summary: Reviewed all five modified files (documentation-only changes): mcp-server/docs/agents/workflow-specification/README.md, mcp-server/docs/agents/workflow-specification/operations.md, mcp-server/AGENTS.md, AGENTS.md (root), mcp-server/docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md.

Maintainability — PASS. All additions are clearly scoped and follow existing documentation conventions. Compliance Model (README.md §Compliance Model) uses a tidy authority hierarchy table with 6 concise, actionable rules. Constraint 0 adheres to the documented constraint template format (Rule / Rationale / Scope sections). Per-constraint traceability blockquotes (Constraints 11/13/19/22) are single-line and unambiguous.

Best Practices — PASS. Changes are DRY: governance text is authored once at the spec README and cross-referenced elsewhere — no spec content is duplicated into AGENTS.md or constraints.md. mcp-server/AGENTS.md row 0 correctly precedes the manifest rows so agents encounter the spec before any implementation document. Root AGENTS.md manifest maintenance row ('Change workflow logic…') correctly mandates spec-first ordering.
Security & Performance — PASS. No code changes. Documentation-only changes cannot introduce vulnerabilities or regressions.

Future Context — PASS. The authority hierarchy (Specification → Implementation → Tests → Manifest → Orchestrator) is architecturally sound and future-proof. Rule 5 ('implementation notes within the spec are illustrative, not authoritative') is a valuable nuance that prevents spec drift when internal code structure changes. The orchestrator is correctly listed as an alternate implementation subject to the same spec — important for multi-runtime consistency.

One pre-existing non-blocking issue confirmed (escalated from QA): Root AGENTS.md navigation row uses the file system path as link text rather than 'Workflow Specification'. This means a workspace search for the two-word phrase returns 4/5 modified files. No new blocking issues introduced. PASS issued.

comments.note: Root AGENTS.md navigation row (line 274): link text is the file path 'mcp-server/docs/agents/workflow-specification/README.md' rather than a human-readable label. QA's suggested fix — change the display text to 'Workflow Specification (workflow-specification/)' or simply 'Workflow Specification' — would (a) align with mcp-server/AGENTS.md manifest table row 0 style, and (b) ensure a workspace search for the two-word phrase returns all five modified files. Non-blocking; correct as-is for navigability, but the cosmetic inconsistency is worth a one-line follow-up fix.

Rule 5 of the Compliance Model ('implementation notes within the spec are illustrative, not authoritative') is architecturally nuanced and well-placed. Consider adding a short concrete example — e.g. '(e.g., if CLAIMABLE_ROLES is refactored into a different module, the spec's algorithmic definition in §10.1 remains authoritative)' — to make the intended distinction immediately clear to future readers without requiring them to look up the operations.md cross-reference.

No cross-cutting issues. All five files are internally consistent. The governance layer (Constraint 0 + Compliance Model + mcp-server/AGENTS.md Constraint 12) forms a well-interlocked triad: agents entering via any of the three paths encounter the spec-first mandate before they can reach mutable workflow logic.
